source.title: Going Beyond Linear Mode Connectivity: The Layerwise Linear Feature Connectivity
source.authors: Zhanpeng Zhou; Yong-Yi Yang; Xiaojiang Yang; Junchi Yan; Wei Hu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure/table formatting is flattened, but the stitching results can be read from the tables.
record.tranche_reason: Tests V4 with a different measure: evaluates whether one network's intermediate activations can be passed directly into another network's later layers, reporting test error by stitching layer. It does not test convergence with scale or cross-modal representation similarity.
record.gate_note: The paper's LLFC cosine results compare an interpolated-weight model's features with the interpolation of the endpoint features; they do not measure alignment between independently trained models as V1–V3 or V6–V7 describe. The reported direct model-stitching results do bear on V4 and are recorded below. Other reported comparisons, including commutativity and weak additivity, do not measure the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: Appendix B.4 feeds network A's layer activations straight into network B's later layers, with no stitching layer, and reports test error by layer. This bears on V4 (interchangeable representations via stitching), but only for spawned pairs: same architecture, same initialization and 5 shared epochs (CIFAR-10), or the same initialization (MLP). The main LLFC results compare an interpolated model's features with interpolated endpoint features. That is not cross-model alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but misweighted. The main conclusion is that LLFC is a prevalent phenomenon co-occurring with LMC (spawning and permutation), arising from weak additivity and commutativity, and that Git Re-Basin can be read as enforcing commutativity. The stitching result is a secondary appendix observation: stitched errors 'closely resemble' the originals, suggesting LLFC models encode similar, cross-decodable information.
record.recipe_differences: Tests interchangeability through direct model stitching without an added trainable stitching layer; the paired models are obtained by spawning. This is not the original representation-distance convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: Stitching layer changes the error rate; results vary substantially by layer, especially for VGG-16 and ResNet-20.

fits_no_version.finding: For linearly mode-connected pairs (spawned or permutation-matched), each layer's features in the weight-interpolated model point the same way as the interpolation of the endpoint features (1−cosine near 0). Independently trained unmatched pairs do not show this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linearly mode-connected networks show layerwise linear feature connectivity, explained by weak ReLU additivity and commutativity between networks.

record.problems: The stitching evidence is limited to image-classification models with identical architectures and spawned endpoints. Results vary by layer, and the paper does not report uncertainty for the stitching error tables. The paper itself says its empirical work mainly focuses on image classification.
record.rows_left_out: None of the stitching results were omitted. LLFC cosine comparisons, commutativity measurements, weak-additivity measurements, and their associated controls were not entered as rows because they do not measure a listed claim version's representation alignment or interchangeability outcome.

untested.parts: No scaling of model size or capability; no comparison across architectures, objectives or data.
No vision-language or paired image-caption alignment.

Stitching uses spawned pairs with shared initialization and early training, not separate initializations. Permutation-matched independent models are analysed only through LLFC, weak additivity and commutativity distances, not through shared-feature or stitching measures.

Only identity stitching (no learned map) between spawned same-architecture image classifiers. Not tested: independently trained or permutation-aligned pairs, learned linear or affine stitching layers, relative representations, mapping without paired data, and cross-architecture mapping.
No interpretable features, circuits or SAE features.
No comparison of similarity metrics, neighbour settings or input distributions.
No plateau analysis and no test of shared data or objectives as the cause of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The spawned pairs share initialization and, for CIFAR-10, 5 epochs of training, so they are far less independent than V4's usual setting. Supports labels should be read as holding for near-identical training lineages only. The authors' claim that errors 'closely resemble' the originals at all layers is stronger than Tables 2–3 show. No uncertainty is reported for the stitching tables.

versions.untested_parts: Model size or capability scaling and alignment across models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions as models improve.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized models, distinct from the paper's feature-linearity property.
The stitching test uses same-architecture image classifiers obtained by spawning; it does not test relative representations, paired-data-free mappings, or other mapping methods.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits such as neurons or SAE features.
Alternative similarity measures, neighbour settings, and input-distribution choices for measuring convergence.
Whether alignment plateaus or is explained by shared training data or objectives rather than a common model of reality.

relationships.condition: Spawned same-architecture pairs, direct stitching at MLP FC 3, VGG-16 Conv 1-1 and Conv 4-1 to FC 2, and ResNet-20 Block 3-3
relationships.reason: Stitched error stays within about 0.1 to 0.7 points of the endpoints (e.g. VGG Conv 5-2 6.88% vs 6.87/7.1%; r3, r4, r11–r18, r27).
relationships.display_finding: Stitched error stayed within about 0.1–0.7 points of endpoint errors, including VGG Conv 5-2 at 6.88% versus 6.87% and 7.1%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Spawned same-architecture pairs, direct stitching at MLP FC 3, VGG-16 Conv 1-1 and Conv 4-1 to FC 2, and ResNet-20 Block 3-3
source_check.reason: The specified layers retain near-endpoint performance without a learned map: Tables 1–3 confirm r3, r4, r11–r18 and r27.

relationships.condition: Spawned pairs, direct stitching at early and middle layers: MLP FC 1–2, VGG-16 Conv 1-2 to 3-3, ResNet-20 Block 1-1 to 3-2
relationships.reason: Error rises clearly above the endpoints at these layers: up to 11.84% vs about 7% for VGG and 13.35% vs about 8.6% for ResNet-20. Interchangeability depends on layer (r1, r2, r5–r10, r19–r26).
relationships.display_finding: Stitched error reached 11.84% versus approximately 7% at VGG endpoints and 13.35% versus approximately 8.6% at ResNet-20 endpoints.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Spawned pairs, direct stitching at early and middle layers: MLP FC 1–2, VGG-16 Conv 1-2 to 3-3, ResNet-20 Block 1-1 to 3-2
source_check.reason: Tables 1–3 show layer-dependent excess error, including VGG-16 11.84% versus 6.87%/7.1% and ResNet-20 13.35% versus 8.69%/8.58%, supporting incomplete direct interchangeability.

relation.reason: The study measures stitched-model test errors against endpoint errors, directly testing interchangeability in spawned pairs.

tranche.reason: Appendix B.4 tests V4 through direct activation stitching without a learned stitching layer, a different method bearing on representation interchangeability.

source_check.notes: Appendix B.1.1 distinguishes MLP pairs spawned from a common initialization from VGG-16/ResNet-20 pairs sharing five training epochs. Stitching tests only spawned pairs without a learned map; it does not establish failure of learned alignment or interchangeability between different architectures.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: VGG-16 layers Conv 1-1 and Conv 4-1 through FC 2; ResNet-20 Block 3-3; and MLP FC 3
reader_labels.reason: Direct cross-network activation transfer without a learned stitching layer yields error rates near the original models at these layers (r3, r4, r11–r18, r27).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MLP FC 1–2; VGG-16 Conv 1-2 through Conv 3-3; and ResNet-20 Block 1-1 through Block 3-2
reader_labels.reason: Transfer remains functional, but several stitching layers incur noticeably higher error than the original models, so interchangeability is not uniformly lossless (r1–r2, r5–r10, r19–r26).
